# R-5's header-transit corpus: D-44's normalization tuple, measured.
#
# The fidelity corpus beside the sanitizer holds bodies, and D-44's tuple is taken over
# headers, so this is its header half, admitted under D-115's rule: every group carries a
# provenance and a source. `constructed` means written for this corpus after a transformation
# that source documents, with every name, address and host on a reserved example domain.
#
# A group is one question. `kind: same` groups are ONE message observed at two or more points
# (as sent, after a relay hop, as a list echoes it, as a server re-presents it); they measure
# SURVIVAL. `kind: distinct` groups are exactly two genuinely different messages that one D-44
# scope could propose together; they measure COLLISION.
#
#   == <group id>                 permanent; never renumbered, reused or removed
#   kind: same | distinct
#   provenance: constructed | captured
#   source: <what documents the transformation or the sender's behaviour>
#   equal: <the tuple elements every observation agrees on, after normalization, or `none`>
#   digest: agrees | diverges     <for `distinct`, `agrees` is a collision>
#   -- <observation label>
#   <raw header lines; a line starting with a space or tab continues the previous one>
#
# `\u{HEX}` in a header line stands for that character, so that a trailing space or a
# decomposed accent survives editors and hooks that would silently normalize the literal.
# Header values reach the tuple unfolded (RFC 5322 s2.2.3) with the whitespace after the colon
# dropped, and with any RFC 2047 encoded word left as written: decoding is the adapter's,
# and no encoded word appears in a field the tuple reads.
#
# `equal` and `digest` are the measurement, recorded. The test recomputes both from the raw
# headers under the current rule version and fails on any difference, so a rule change that
# moves a result has to move it here too, where the change is visible.
#
# Elements: from, date, subject, references.

== relay-hop-unchanged
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5321 s3.7.2 (a relay adds trace fields and does not alter the message's own headers) and RFC 6376 (a signing hop adds a signature field)
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent
From: Sam Example <sam@example.test>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2026 09:14:02 +0100
Subject: Bounded queue options
Message-ID: <q1@mail.example.test>
References: <q0@mail.example.test>
In-Reply-To: <q0@mail.example.test>
-- after two hops
Return-Path: <sam@example.test>
Received: from mx2.example.net by mx1.example.org; Tue, 16 Sep 2026 08:14:04 +0000
Received: from out.example.test by mx2.example.net; Tue, 16 Sep 2026 08:14:03 +0000
DKIM-Signature: v=1; a=rsa-sha256; d=example.test; s=s1; h=from:date:subject; b=AAAA
Authentication-Results: mx1.example.org; dkim=pass header.d=example.test
From: Sam Example <sam@example.test>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2026 09:14:02 +0100
Subject: Bounded queue options
Message-ID: <q1@mail.example.test>
References: <q0@mail.example.test>
In-Reply-To: <q0@mail.example.test>

== refold-at-space
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5322 s2.2.3 (a long field may be folded at any existing whitespace; unfolding removes only the line break)
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent, one line
From: ops@example.test
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2026 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: Quarterly capacity review for the storage cluster and the two replica sites in the north region
-- refolded by a relay
From: ops@example.test
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2026 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: Quarterly capacity review for the storage cluster
 and the two replica sites in the north region

== refold-with-tab
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5322 s2.2.3 (folding white space is a space or a horizontal tab); gateways that fold with a tab, which unfolds to a tab where the sender wrote a space
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent, one line
From: ops@example.test
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2026 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Quarterly capacity review for the storage cluster and the two replica sites
-- refolded with a tab
From: ops@example.test
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2026 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Quarterly capacity review for the storage cluster and the two
	replica sites

== refold-inserting-space
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5322 s2.2.3 permits folding only at existing whitespace; a non-compliant folder that inserts its own space leaves a doubled space after unfolding
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent
From: ops@example.test
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2026 10:10:00 +0000
Subject: Replica lag alert summary for the north region
-- refolded with an inserted space
From: ops@example.test
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2026 10:10:00 +0000
Subject: Replica lag alert summary for the
  north region

== trailing-whitespace-stripped
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5321 s4.5.3 and transport gateways that strip trailing white space from header lines
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent, with trailing spaces
From: billing@example.test
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2026 07:30:00 +0000
Subject: Your invoice for September\u{20}\u{20}
-- trailing spaces stripped in transit
From: billing@example.test
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2026 07:30:00 +0000
Subject: Your invoice for September

== invisible-character-inserted
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: gateways and clients that insert a zero-width space or byte-order mark into a subject, the insertion NFR-54 strips before display
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent
From: billing@example.test
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2026 07:45:00 +0000
Subject: Payment received
-- with a zero-width space and a byte-order mark
From: billing@example.test
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2026 07:45:00 +0000
Subject: \u{feff}Payment\u{200b} received

== references-refolded
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5322 s3.6.4 (References is a whitespace-separated list and is folded freely when long)
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent, one line
From: lee@example.test
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2026 16:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Bounded queue options
References: <q0@mail.example.test> <q1@mail.example.test> <q2@mail.example.test> <q3@mail.example.test>
In-Reply-To: <q3@mail.example.test>
-- refolded across three lines
From: lee@example.test
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2026 16:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Bounded queue options
References: <q0@mail.example.test>
	<q1@mail.example.test>
 <q2@mail.example.test>  <q3@mail.example.test>
In-Reply-To: <q3@mail.example.test>

== date-rewritten-to-relay-zone
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5322 s3.3 (one instant, any zone) and gateways that re-emit Date in their own zone and drop the zone comment
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent
From: lee@example.test
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2026 16:45:10 -0700 (PDT)
Subject: Deploy window
-- re-emitted in UTC
From: lee@example.test
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2026 23:45:10 +0000
Subject: Deploy window
-- re-emitted without the day name
From: lee@example.test
Date: 20 Sep 2026 01:45:10 +0200
Subject: Deploy window

== date-obsolete-zone-name
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5322 s4.3 (the obsolete zone names; GMT and UT are +0000)
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent
From: legacy@example.test
Date: Sat, 20 Sep 2026 12:00:00 GMT
Subject: Nightly batch report
-- normalized by a relay
From: legacy@example.test
Date: Sat, 20 Sep 2026 12:00:00 +0000
Subject: Nightly batch report

== from-case-and-display-name
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5321 s2.4 (a domain is case-insensitive) and gateways that re-quote or re-encode the display name
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent
From: "Example, Sam" <Sam@Example.TEST>
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2026 08:00:00 +0000
Subject: Weekend on-call handover
-- re-emitted by a gateway
From: =?utf-8?q?Example=2C_Sam?= <sam@example.test>
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2026 08:00:00 +0000
Subject: Weekend on-call handover

== from-obsolete-comment-form
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5322 s4.4 (the obsolete address-with-comment form) rewritten to name-addr by a gateway
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- as sent
From: sam@example.test (Sam Example)
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Handover notes
-- rewritten
From: Sam Example <sam@example.test>
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Handover notes

== subject-renormalized
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: Unicode normalization forms; a client that stores the decomposed form (NFD) of what the sender wrote composed (NFC)
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- composed
From: chloe@example.test
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2026 11:00:00 +0200
Subject: Réunion café à 15h
-- decomposed
From: chloe@example.test
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2026 11:00:00 +0200
Subject: Re\u{301}union cafe\u{301} a\u{300} 15h

== list-subject-tag
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: list managers that prefix the list's tag to the subject of the copy they redistribute (Mailman subject_prefix)
equal: from, date, references
digest: diverges
-- the sender's own sent copy
From: sam@example.test
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2026 09:00:00 +0000
Subject: Release branch cut on Thursday
-- the list's copy in the same mailbox
From: sam@example.test
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2026 09:00:00 +0000
Subject: [dev] Release branch cut on Thursday
List-Id: <dev.lists.example.test>

== list-from-rewritten
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 7960 s4.1.3 (a list rewrites From to its own address so its redistribution passes the sender's DMARC policy)
equal: date, subject, references
digest: diverges
-- the sender's own sent copy
From: Sam Example <sam@example.test>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Freeze starts Friday
-- the list's copy
From: "Sam Example via dev" <dev@lists.example.test>
Reply-To: Sam Example <sam@example.test>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Freeze starts Friday

== list-tag-and-from-rewritten
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 7960 s4.1.3 together with a subject prefix, the common configuration of a list that must pass DMARC
equal: date, references
digest: diverges
-- the sender's own sent copy
From: sam@example.test
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2026 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Freeze starts Friday
References: <f0@mail.example.test>
In-Reply-To: <f0@mail.example.test>
-- the list's copy
From: "Sam Example via dev" <dev@lists.example.test>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2026 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: [dev] Re: Freeze starts Friday
References: <f0@mail.example.test>
In-Reply-To: <f0@mail.example.test>

== resent-copy
kind: same
provenance: constructed
source: RFC 5322 s3.6.6 (a resent message keeps the original's fields and adds Resent- fields)
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- the original
From: sam@example.test
Date: Wed, 24 Sep 2026 14:00:00 +0000
Subject: Contract draft
-- redirected into the same mailbox
Resent-From: assistant@example.test
Resent-Date: Wed, 24 Sep 2026 15:10:00 +0000
From: sam@example.test
Date: Wed, 24 Sep 2026 14:00:00 +0000
Subject: Contract draft

== duplicate-id-device-different-minute
kind: distinct
provenance: constructed
source: senders that reuse one fixed Message-ID for every message (appliances, scanners), the duplication R-5 names; two scans a minute apart
equal: from, subject, references
digest: diverges
-- first scan
From: scanner@office.example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 09:00:01 +0000
Subject: Scanned document
Message-ID: <1@localhost>
-- second scan
From: scanner@office.example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 09:01:12 +0000
Subject: Scanned document
Message-ID: <1@localhost>

== duplicate-id-device-same-second
kind: distinct
provenance: constructed
source: the same appliance as duplicate-id-device-different-minute, sending two scans within one second
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- first scan
From: scanner@office.example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 09:05:30 +0000
Subject: Scanned document
Message-ID: <1@localhost>
-- second scan
From: scanner@office.example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 09:05:30 +0000
Subject: Scanned document
Message-ID: <1@localhost>

== automated-no-date
kind: distinct
provenance: constructed
source: automated senders that omit Date where no submission server adds one (RFC 6409 s8.3 makes adding it optional); two alerts hours apart
equal: from, date, subject, references
digest: agrees
-- morning alert
From: cron@host.example.test
Subject: Backup job failed
-- evening alert
From: cron@host.example.test
Subject: Backup job failed

== notification-same-subject
kind: distinct
provenance: constructed
source: transactional senders that send one fixed subject for every message of a kind
equal: from, subject, references
digest: diverges
-- first code
From: no-reply@auth.example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 12:00:00 +0000
Subject: Your verification code
-- second code, thirty seconds later
From: no-reply@auth.example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 12:00:30 +0000
Subject: Your verification code

== two-replies-to-one-parent
kind: distinct
provenance: constructed
source: two replies by one person to the same message, a minute apart, which share the subject and the whole reference chain
equal: from, subject, references
digest: diverges
-- first reply
From: lee@example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 13:00:05 +0000
Subject: Re: Deploy window
References: <d0@mail.example.test>
In-Reply-To: <d0@mail.example.test>
-- second reply
From: lee@example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 13:01:40 +0000
Subject: Re: Deploy window
References: <d0@mail.example.test>
In-Reply-To: <d0@mail.example.test>

== absent-versus-empty-subject
kind: distinct
provenance: constructed
source: a message with no Subject field and one with an empty Subject field, otherwise alike
equal: from, date, references
digest: diverges
-- no subject field
From: sam@example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 14:00:00 +0000
-- an empty subject field
From: sam@example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 14:00:00 +0000
Subject:

== same-second-different-sender
kind: distinct
provenance: constructed
source: one fixed subject sent by two senders in one second, as a service fanning out from two hosts does
equal: date, subject, references
digest: diverges
-- first host
From: alerts@a.example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 15:00:00 +0000
Subject: Disk usage above 90%
-- second host
From: alerts@b.example.test
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2026 15:00:00 +0000
Subject: Disk usage above 90%
